title: DEIM-S vs D-FINE-S: measured on the same protocol
dek: DEIM-S and D-FINE-S share 10.32M parameters; on the same COCO protocol D-FINE-S measures 1.3 mAP points higher on desktop GPU.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: D-FINE-S and DEIM-S are the same size: 10.32M parameters, 141.6 MB peak VRAM, both at 640 px. On an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, D-FINE-S measures 1.3 mAP points higher, 53.4 vs 52.1 mAP@50-95, and the two run within one FPS of each other. The newer DEIM-S does not overtake D-FINE-S on this protocol.

DEIM-S (released 2024-12-05) is the later model; D-FINE-S (2024-10-18) is the earlier one. Both are Apache-2.0 and share the same parameter count, so this is a like-for-like accuracy and speed comparison.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. DEIM-S and D-FINE-S highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. D-FINE-S measures 53.4 mAP@50-95 to DEIM-S's 52.1, a 1.3 point difference. D-FINE-S also edges ahead on small objects: 37.9 vs 36.0 mAP_small. The gap is small enough that either model covers the same accuracy tier.

In PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti, the two are close: D-FINE-S at 34.2 FPS, DEIM-S at 33.4. The order stays tight under conversion, 98.7 vs 97.6 FPS on TensorRT FP32 and 86.5 vs 82.4 FPS on TensorRT FP16. On Jetson Orin both land near 10 FPS.
The ranking is stable. D-FINE-S stays ahead on accuracy across 4 runtimes and 3 hardware platforms with verified data, down to the Raspberry Pi 5, where both run 1.1 FPS.

Pick D-FINE-S for a small margin more accuracy at the same memory and speed cost. Pick DEIM-S if it is already in the pipeline: it matches D-FINE-S closely enough that switching for accuracy alone is not worth it. Both are Apache-2.0, so licensing does not decide it.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

deim = LibreYOLO("LibreDEIMs.pt")    # 10.32M params, 52.1 mAP@50-95
dfine = LibreYOLO("LibreDFINEs.pt")  # 10.32M params, 53.4 mAP@50-95

results = dfine("image.jpg")
